objects.description: No custom types are defined in this header. This umbrella header only includes other YARA headers and contains no struct/enum/typedef/class definitions of its own. Any types such as YR_COMPILER, YR_RULES, etc., are defined in the included headers, not here, and therefore are out of scope per the instructions.
Transition code type used by macros to encode state transitions in the Aho–Corasick automaton. Not defined in this header; likely an integer type defined elsewhere. Details unknown in this file.
Opaque Aho–Corasick automaton handle manipulated via the yr_ac_* API in this header. The concrete struct/class definition is not present here.
Memory arena handle used to allocate and store automaton data. Not defined in this header; concrete layout unknown here.
String metadata object for YARA rules used when adding patterns to the automaton. Not defined in this header.
Atom list node used to represent atoms extracted from a string for the automaton building process. Not defined in this header.
Built-in 32-bit unsigned integer type used as a parameter (string index). Included here only if explicitly typedef’d in this header, which it is not. Not a custom type.

objects.definition: typedef uint32_t yr_arena_off_t;
objects.description: Unsigned 32-bit offset type used for addressing within arena buffers. Offsets are limited to 4 GiB to match 32-bit fields in YR_ARENA_REF and on-disk format.

Owns a set of growable buffers and relocation metadata. Provides allocation, write, reference <-> pointer translation, and relocatable-pointer tracking for data stored across up to YR_MAX_ARENA_BUFFERS buffers. Lifetime is ref-counted via yr_arena_acquire/release.
Internal arena buffer descriptor containing the data pointer, total capacity, and used length. Managed by YR_ARENA; not independently constructed/destroyed by API.
Packed 8-byte reference identifying a location inside an arena by buffer id and offset. Used in place of raw pointers for stability across buffer reallocations and for serialization.
Singly-linked list node describing a relocatable pointer location within an arena buffer, enabling fix-ups when buffers move. Managed internally by YR_ARENA.

Atom used by YARA to represent a fixed-length byte pattern with an associated mask. length is the number of meaningful bytes; bytes holds the atom data; mask indicates per-byte which bits are significant. Likely used as the minimal matching unit extracted from regexes/strings for scanning.

Node within an atom tree. type is one of ATOM_TREE_LEAF/AND/OR; atom is the data for leaf nodes; re_nodes maps each atom byte to its originating RE node; children_* form a linked list of child nodes; next_sibling links siblings. Used to represent boolean combinations of atoms derived from regex ASTs.
Container for an atom tree with a single root node. Encapsulates boolean structure over atoms for efficient matching.
Linked-list node holding a single atom plus metadata: backtrack distance and arena references to compiled forward/backward code. next links to the following item.
Packed table entry mapping a specific atom byte sequence to a quality score. Used by quality evaluation functions to score atoms.

objects.definition: typedef int (*YR_ATOMS_QUALITY_FUNC)(YR_ATOMS_CONFIG* config, YR_ATOM* atom);
objects.description: Function pointer type for computing the quality score of a given atom under a provided configuration. Returns an int score.

Configuration for atom extraction and scoring. Holds the quality function, optional quality lookup table and its size, a warning threshold, and ownership flag indicating whether the table should be freed by the config.
Referenced pointer type representing a regex AST node from <yara/re.h>. Only forward-referenced here; definition not present in this header.
Referenced pointer type representing a regex AST from <yara/re.h>. Only referenced by function prototypes; definition not present here.

Referenced type for modifiers applied during atom extraction (e.g., ASCII/WIDE/NOCASE). Only referenced in function prototypes; definition not present in this header.

Linked-list node used to represent segments of a Base64 pattern. Each node holds a pointer to a sized string (the segment), a flag indicating whether the segment was escaped, and a pointer to the next node. Intended for building/iterating a chain of Base64 tokens during parsing.

Linked-list node holding a reference to a string stored in the arena (via YR_ARENA_REF) and a pointer to the next element. Used to build string sets during compilation.
Container for a set of strings implemented as a singly linked list, tracking total count and head pointer. The memory for string data resides in the arena referenced by each element.

Represents a parsed expression in the compiler, carrying its type and a union with literal value/object/arena-ref. Also stores requirements for string counts in boolean contexts and an associated identifier either as a direct pointer or arena reference.
Function pointer type for compiler diagnostics callbacks invoked with error/warning level, location, associated rule, message, and opaque user data.
Function pointer type for handling include directives during compilation. Returns a pointer to included content (to be later freed by include_free).
Function pointer type used to free the memory returned by the include callback.
Function pointer type for receiving the regular-expression AST for a given rule/string during compilation.
Linked-list node used to track locations in the arena/code that require fixup (backpatching) after more information is available.
Holds per-loop compilation state: start location for back-jumps, declared loop-local variables with their expression metadata, and count of internal variables used by the compiler.

Main compiler state object used by YARA during rule compilation. Manages the arena sections, indices of current items under compilation, error handling, automata/tables, include stack, loop contexts, callbacks, and configuration. Lifetime is managed via yr_compiler_create/destroy. Not thread-safe unless externally synchronized.

Represents a memory-mapped file region created by the YARA file mapping utilities. Holds the originating file descriptor/handle, the mapped size, a const pointer to the mapped bytes, and on Windows a HANDLE to the mapping object. Used with yr_filemap_map/yr_filemap_map_fd/yr_filemap_map_ex to create mappings and yr_filemap_unmap/yr_filemap_unmap_fd to release them. The data pointer should be treated as read-only; unmap before closing the underlying file handle when using the fd-specific APIs.

Hash table bucket entry node storing a key (raw pointer with explicit length), an optional namespace string (ns), the associated value pointer, and a next pointer for separate chaining within a bucket. Keys can be arbitrary binary data; when using string keys, the raw key APIs are also available. Memory ownership and lifetimes of key/value are managed by caller; cleanup can be performed via provided free callback when cleaning/destroying the table.

Open-hashed hash table structure with a fixed number of buckets (size) and an array of bucket head pointers. The buckets array is declared with size 1 as a flexible array placeholder; real allocations provide space for size bucket pointers. Collisions are resolved via linked lists of YR_HASH_TABLE_ENTRY nodes.

Statistics structure for a YR_RULES set (e.g., scan counters, timings). Only referenced here; defined elsewhere.
Represents a single compiled YARA rule. Only referenced here; defined elsewhere. Can be enabled/disabled.
Arena allocator/serialization container for YARA’s internal data. Only referenced here; defined elsewhere. Used to build YR_RULES via yr_rules_from_arena.

Opaque/forward-declared scan context type referenced in this header via a pointer. The concrete definition is not present in this file; it is likely defined elsewhere (e.g., in another YARA header or source file). It represents per-scan state used during matching/verification.
Opaque/forward-declared Aho–Corasick match record type referenced here via a pointer. The actual structure is defined elsewhere. It likely encapsulates pattern-match metadata used by the scanner.

Rule object used by the scanner. This header only references it; no definition is provided here. Details and lifetime management are defined elsewhere in YARA.
String object associated with a YARA rule, referenced for error reporting. Only referenced here; not defined in this header.
Per-rule profiling information structure used for performance reporting. Only referenced here; definition is external to this header.
Compiled set of YARA rules used to initialize a scanner. Only referenced here; not defined in this header.
Iterator over memory blocks for scanning. Only referenced here; not defined in this header.
File descriptor type used by YARA portability layer. Only referenced here; not defined in this header.

Growable dynamic string object holding current length (len), capacity in bytes (cap), and a heap-allocated C string buffer (str) that is likely NUL-terminated. Provides a lightweight, readable interface for formatted construction and append operations. Ownership of the internal buffer can be transferred via sstr_move. Exact allocation, growth strategy, and NUL-termination guarantees are inferred but not explicitly documented here.

Referenced from <yara/types.h>; not defined in this header. Ignored per instructions.

Packed, length-prefixed string structure that allows embedded NUL bytes. It stores the byte length and flags, followed by a NUL-terminated char data buffer declared as a 1-byte flexible tail (classic struct hack). Flags include SIZED_STRING_FLAGS_NO_CASE (1) and SIZED_STRING_FLAGS_DOT_ALL (2) for case-insensitive and dot-all regex semantics. Allocation must account for length+1 bytes of c_string. Unknown alignment constraints beyond #pragma pack(1).

Opaque-typedef plus full struct defining a generic, heap-backed stack container. It stores items in a growable array, tracking capacity, per-item size, and the index of the current top. Items are treated as raw memory blocks of size item_size. Ownership/lifetime is managed via the provided API: create, destroy, push, pop.

Platform-specific stopwatch state used to measure elapsed time in nanoseconds. On Windows it stores performance counter frequency and start value. On Apple it stores mach timebase info and the start tick. On other POSIX systems it stores either a timeval or timespec union for the start time. Used with yr_stopwatch_start and yr_stopwatch_elapsed_ns to measure intervals. Construction is implicit via stack or allocation; initialize by calling yr_stopwatch_start before measuring. Destruction has no special requirements.

Abstraction of an operating system thread identifier. On Windows it aliases DWORD; on POSIX it aliases pthread_t. Used to represent the current thread id via yr_current_thread_id. Details such as lifetime and value range are platform-dependent.

Key/handle for thread-local storage (TLS). Maps to DWORD on Windows and pthread_key_t on POSIX. Use the yr_thread_storage_* API to create, destroy, and get/set per-thread values associated with this key.
Cross-platform mutex abstraction. On Windows it aliases HANDLE; on POSIX it aliases pthread_mutex_t. Use the yr_mutex_* API to create, destroy, lock, and unlock.

Node in a regular-expression AST. Stores node type, parameters, greediness, optional class, sibling/child links, and code references for forward/backward matching.
Character class used by regex engine. A 256-bit bitmap with a negation flag indicates membership of bytes in the class.
Container for regex-related error messages up to 383 chars plus NUL.

Doubly-linked list endpoints for RE_FIBER scheduling in the regex engine.
Pool of reusable RE_FIBER objects for regex execution.
Node used by the fast regex executor to track explored positions/rounds over input with double links.

Node/state in the Aho–Corasick automaton. Links for trie and failure edges, reference to its match list in arena, depth/input byte, and transition-table slot.
Aho–Corasick automaton holder with arena, transition-table sizing/packing helpers, usage bitmask, and root state pointer.

Rule namespace descriptor with name (arena reference) and its index within the namespaces table. 8-byte aligned idx for MSVC 32-bit layout stability.
Metadata entry attached to a rule: identifier name, optional string value or integer value, with type and flags. Identifier and string are arena-backed references.
Container for a doubly-linked list of YR_MATCH with a count. Used per-string to track matches during scanning.

Compiled rule string with flags, indexes, optional fixed offset, raw bytes pointer, chain linkage for split strings with gap constraints, and identifier. Many fields are stored via arena references for relocatability.
Compiled rule header with flags, atom stats, required-strings mask count, and arena references to identifier, tags, metas, strings, and owning namespace.

Simple summary of a compiled ruleset with counts of rules, strings, and namespaces.

functions.name: yr_ac_automaton_create
functions.description: Creates and initializes an empty Aho–Corasick (AC) automaton object, allocating its internal structures using the provided arena. Returns a status code (library-specific). Typically called once at setup before adding strings and compiling. The created automaton is returned via the out-parameter.
requirements: arena must point to a valid, initialized YR_ARENA capable of allocating the automaton’s internal data (inferred from parameter type and name).
automaton must be a non-null pointer to a YR_AC_AUTOMATON* (an out-parameter); on success, *automaton references the newly created automaton (standard C out-parameter convention).
Must be called before yr_ac_add_string and yr_ac_compile (inferred from typical AC workflow).
The arena’s lifetime must extend at least through the automaton’s use (inferred from use of arena for allocation).
Check and handle the returned int error code; specific values are library-defined (explicitly unknown).

functions.name: yr_ac_automaton_destroy
functions.description: Destroys a previously created AC automaton and releases its associated resources. Returns a status code (library-specific). Use after you are done using the automaton.
requirements: automaton must be a valid pointer to an automaton previously returned by yr_ac_automaton_create (inferred from naming).
Do not use the automaton after destruction (inferred).
Caller must check and handle the returned int error code; specific values are library-defined (explicitly unknown).

functions.signature: int yr_ac_add_string(YR_AC_AUTOMATON* automaton, YR_STRING* string, uint32_t string_idx, YR_ATOM_LIST_ITEM* atom, YR_ARENA* arena);
functions.description: Adds a YR_STRING pattern to the AC automaton, associating it with the caller-supplied string index and atom information. Allocations for the new trie nodes or metadata are performed from the provided arena. Call this for each pattern before compiling the automaton. Returns a status code (library-specific).
requirements: automaton must be a valid automaton created by yr_ac_automaton_create (inferred).

functions.signature: #define yr_bitmask_set(bm, i) do { (bm)[(i) / YR_BITMASK_SLOT_BITS] |= 1UL << ((i) % YR_BITMASK_SLOT_BITS); } while (0)

functions.description: Macro that clears bit i (0-based) in a YR_BITMASK bitmap. The bitmap is represented as an array of YR_BITMASK slots.

functions.name: yr_mutex_create
functions.description: Initializes a YR_MUTEX object for later synchronization use. It wraps platform mutex creation (HANDLE on Windows, pthread_mutex_t on POSIX). Returns an int status code; exact success/error conventions are not documented here.
requirements: Argument must be a non-null pointer to writable storage for a YR_MUTEX.

functions.name: yr_mutex_destroy

requirements: Argument must be a non-null pointer to a previously initialized YR_MUTEX created by yr_mutex_create.

functions.name: yr_mutex_lock

The mutex storage must remain valid while locking.

Which thread may lock/unlock is not specified; by convention, the same thread that locks should unlock.

functions.name: yr_mutex_unlock
functions.description: Releases (unlocks) a previously locked YR_MUTEX. Returns an int status code; exact success/error conventions are not documented here.
requirements: Argument must be a non-null pointer to an initialized YR_MUTEX created by yr_mutex_create.
The mutex should have been successfully locked before by some thread; whether it must be the same thread is not specified here (commonly required).

functions.name: yr_thread_storage_create
functions.description: Creates a thread-local storage (TLS) key usable with yr_thread_storage_set_value and yr_thread_storage_get_value. Wraps platform TLS key creation (DWORD TLS index on Windows, pthread_key_t on POSIX). Returns an int status code; exact conventions are not documented here.

functions.name: yr_thread_storage_set_value

functions.name: yr_thread_storage_get_value
functions.description: Retrieves the per-thread pointer value previously set for the calling thread and the given TLS key. If no value was set, the return may be NULL or an unspecified default; exact semantics are not documented here.

import os

from typing import List

# Generator for a generic binary blob to seed multiple YARA-related fuzz stubs.
# Goals based on stubs:
# - Provide varied, but valid, byte buffers suitable for:
#   * Streams (read/write) with internal structure and mixed sizes
#   * Entry point parsers (yr_get_entry_point_offset/address): include PE/ELF/Mach-O like headers occasionally
#   * Hashing (arbitrary data, sometimes empty)
#   * memmem, unaligned accessors: ensure sufficient lengths and internal patterns
#   * Atoms/string related paths: include ASCII text, wide strings, base64-like, binary noise
# - Keep size <= 4096 bytes
# - Deterministic with seed, but randomized per call

ASCII_WORDS = [
    b"rule test { condition: true }\n",
    b"rule r1 { strings: $a = " + b"A"*8 + b" condition: $a }\n",
    b"hello world\n",
    b"The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog\n",
    b"include \"mod\"\n",
    b"namespace foo\n",
]

BASE64_CHARS = b"ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789+/"


def _rnd(r: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(r.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))


def _make_pe_like(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Minimal PE-like: DOS header + PE signature + COFF + optional header stub
    # Not strictly valid, but shaped enough for entry-point code paths.
    dos = bytearray(64)
    dos[0:2] = b"MZ"
    e_lfanew = 0x80
    struct.pack_into("<I", dos, 0x3C, e_lfanew)
    pad = b"\x00" * (e_lfanew - len(dos)) if e_lfanew > len(dos) else b""
    nt = bytearray()
    nt += b"PE\x00\x00"
    # COFF header (20 bytes)
    nt += struct.pack("<HHIIIHH", 0x14c, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0xE0, 0x102)
    # Optional header magic PE32/PE32+
    is_plus = r.choice([False, True])
    if is_plus:
        nt += struct.pack("<H", 0x20B)
        nt += _rnd(r, 0xE0-2)
    else:
        nt += struct.pack("<H", 0x10B)
        nt += _rnd(r, 0xE0-2)
    body = bytes(dos) + pad + bytes(nt)
    body += _rnd(r, r.randrange(128, 256))
    return body


def _make_elf_like(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Minimal ELF header shape
    e_ident = bytearray(16)
    e_ident[0:4] = b"\x7FELF"
    e_ident[4] = r.choice([1, 2])  # class 32/64
    e_ident[5] = r.choice([1, 2])  # data little/big
    e_ident[6] = 1                 # version
    hdr = bytearray(e_ident)
    hdr += _rnd(r, 48)
    segs = _rnd(r, r.randrange(96, 192))
    return bytes(hdr + segs)


def _make_macho_like(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Minimal Mach-O magic + a few random bytes
    magic = r.choice([0xFEEDFACE, 0xFEEDFACF, 0xCEFAEDFE, 0xCFFAEDFE])
    hdr = struct.pack("<I", magic) + _rnd(r, r.randrange(60, 120))
    return hdr


def _make_wide_string(r: random.Random, s: bytes) -> bytes:
    wide = bytearray()
    for ch in s:
        wide.append(ch)
        wide.append(0)
    wide += b"\x00\x00"  # terminator
    return bytes(wide)


def _make_base64(r: random.Random, length: int) -> bytes:
    n = max(4, length - (length % 4))
    return bytes(r.choice(BASE64_CHARS) for _ in range(n))


def _make_stream_blob(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Mix of segments to exercise stream reads/writes and memmem
    parts: List[bytes] = []
    # Segment 1: ASCII text or YARA rule
    parts.append(r.choice(ASCII_WORDS))
    # Segment 2: base64-like
    parts.append(_make_base64(r, r.randrange(16, 128)))
    # Segment 3: repeated pattern for memmem hits
    token = r.choice([b"AAAA", b"abcd", b"\x00\x01\x02\x03"]) * r.randrange(2, 8)
    parts.append(token)
    # Segment 4: random noise
    parts.append(_rnd(r, r.randrange(32, 256)))
    # Segment 5: optionally a wide string
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        parts.append(_make_wide_string(r, b"WideTest"))
    return b"".join(parts)


def _compose_blob(r: random.Random, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    # Choose a high-level profile
    profile = r.randrange(0, 6)
    if profile == 0:
        core = _make_pe_like(r)
    elif profile == 1:
        core = _make_elf_like(r)
    elif profile == 2:
        core = _make_macho_like(r)
    elif profile == 3:
        core = _make_stream_blob(r)
    elif profile == 4:
        # Pure random bytes with a few aligned/int fields to help unaligned readers
        core = bytearray()
        core += _rnd(r, r.randrange(32, 128))
        # Insert some integers at random offsets
        for _ in range(r.randrange(2, 6)):
            val32 = r.getrandbits(32)
            off = r.randrange(0, max(1, len(core)))
            core[off:off] = struct.pack("<I", val32)
        core = bytes(core)
    else:
        # Mixed: header-ish + stream blob
        core = _make_pe_like(r) + _make_stream_blob(r)

    # Optionally prefix/suffix with random paddings to create more offsets
    if r.random() < 0.7:
        core = _rnd(r, r.randrange(0, 64)) + core
    if r.random() < 0.7:
        core = core + _rnd(r, r.randrange(0, 64))

    # Ensure overall size limit
    if len(core) > max_len:
        core = core[:max_len]

    # Occasionally return an empty blob for APIs that accept len==0
    if r.random() < 0.05:
        return b""
    return core


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed ^ 0x9E3779B97F4A7C15)
    # Total size limit 4096
    blob = _compose_blob(r, 4096)
    # Guarantee non-empty most of the time for consumers expecting data
    if not blob:
        # minimal non-empty buffer with a small pattern and some noise
        blob = b"\x7FELF" + _rnd(r, r.randrange(8, 64))
    return blob

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Data type: C string (NUL-terminated). Our buffer should contain bytes ending with a single \0.
# Goal: Provide interesting yet valid C strings to exercise fuzzer stubs that:
#  - require identifiers [A-Za-z0-9_]
#  - require module names / namespaces
#  - require YARA rule texts
#  - require hex strings, possibly with 0x prefix
#  - require numeric formats for printf
#  - require small/large sizes, boundary lengths, embedded ASCII, etc.
# We will construct a corpus-like generator that, based on the seed, selects a themed
# C-string and returns it as bytes including the terminating NUL.
# The fuzzer will feed this same buffer to multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR / FILENAME, so
# the string should be broadly useful and valid for different consumers.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

_ident_chars = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_"
_printable_no_nul = ''.join(ch for ch in string.printable if ch != '\x0b' and ch != '\x0c' and ch != '\x00')


def _rand_ident(rng: random.Random, min_len=1, max_len=24) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    s = ''.join(rng.choice(_ident_chars) for _ in range(n))
    # Ensure first char is not a digit (good for identifiers)
    if s and s[0].isdigit():
        s = '_' + s[1:]
    return s


def _rand_ns(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Namespace can be empty sometimes, but we keep it non-empty by default
    if rng.random() < 0.1:
        return ""
    parts = [ _rand_ident(rng, 1, rng.randint(3, 10)) for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 3)) ]
    return '::'.join(parts)


def _rand_hex(rng: random.Random, min_digits=1, max_digits=64, with_prefix_prob=0.5) -> str:
    digits = '0123456789abcdef'
    n = rng.randint(min_digits, max_digits)
    s = ''.join(rng.choice(digits) for _ in range(n))
    if rng.random() < with_prefix_prob:
        s = '0x' + s
    return s


def _rand_rule_string(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Produce a valid YARA rule text exercising strings/conditions.
    # Keep it small and syntactically valid.
    ns = _rand_ident(rng, 3, 10)
    rid = _rand_ident(rng, 3, 12)
    sid = _rand_ident(rng, 3, 10)
    lit = ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + " _-.") for _ in range(rng.randint(4, 20)))
    cond = rng.choice([
        f"any of them",
        f"1 of ( {sid}* )".replace('*',''),  # ensure simple id
        f"{sid}",
        "true",
    ])
    # include optional meta and external usage
    ext_name = _rand_ident(rng, 3, 8)
    use_ext = rng.random() < 0.4
    meta = "    meta:\n      author = \"gen\"\n" if rng.random() < 0.5 else ""
    strings = f"    strings:\n      ${sid} = \"{lit}\"\n"
    condition = f"    condition:\n      {cond if not use_ext else f'{sid} and {ext_name} == 1'}\n"
    ns_line = f"namespace {ns}\n" if rng.random() < 0.4 else ""
    rule = (
        f"{ns_line}rule {rid} {{\n" +
        meta +
        strings +
        condition +
        "}\n"
    )
    return rule


def _rand_printf_payload(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # String that can be safely used with %s / %d / %u formats, but is plain text.
    a = _rand_ident(rng, 1, 16)
    b = str(rng.randint(-2**31, 2**31-1))
    c = str(rng.randint(0, 2**32-1))
    return f"{a}-{b}-{c}"


def _rand_cstring(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Select a theme
    theme = rng.choice([
        'identifier', 'namespace', 'hex', 'rule', 'printf', 'path', 'module', 'keyword', 'atom', 'longtext'
    ])

    if theme == 'identifier':
        return _rand_ident(rng, 1, 24)
    if theme == 'namespace':
        return _rand_ns(rng)
    if theme == 'hex':
        return _rand_hex(rng, 1, 64, with_prefix_prob=0.7)
    if theme == 'rule':
        return _rand_rule_string(rng)
    if theme == 'printf':
        return _rand_printf_payload(rng)
    if theme == 'path':
        # plausible filename for FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME (framework writes the file)
        parts = [_rand_ident(rng,1,8) for _ in range(rng.randint(1,3))]
        name = _rand_ident(rng,3,10)
        ext = rng.choice(['yar','yara','txt','dat','bin'])
        return '/' + '/'.join(parts) + '/' + name + '.' + ext
    if theme == 'module':
        # Common YARA modules
        return rng.choice(['pe','elf','macho','cuckoo','math','hash','dotnet'])
    if theme == 'keyword':
        return rng.choice(['true','false','and','or','not','any','all'])
    if theme == 'atom':
        # bytes often used in atoms or base64 alphabet subset
        alpha = 'ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789+/'
        n = rng.randint(4, 32)
        return ''.join(rng.choice(alpha) for _ in range(n))
    if theme == 'longtext':
        n = rng.randint(32, 512)
        return ''.join(rng.choice(_printable_no_nul) for _ in range(n))
    return "x"


def _ensure_nul_terminated(s: str) -> bytes:
    b = s.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore')
    # Limit total size
    if len(b) + 1 > MAX_TOTAL:
        b = b[:MAX_TOTAL-1]
    if not b or b[-1] != 0:
        b += b"\x00"
    return b


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Build a small bundle of multiple C-strings concatenated with NULs to give
    # the fuzzer varied pulls from the same buffer (many frameworks advance internally
    # or slice). Keep total under MAX_TOTAL.
    pieces: List[bytes] = []

    # Always include a valid YARA rule text first (useful for compiler_add_* stubs)
    pieces.append(_ensure_nul_terminated(_rand_rule_string(rng)))

    # Include an identifier and a namespace
    pieces.append(_ensure_nul_terminated(_rand_ident(rng)))
    pieces.append(_ensure_nul_terminated(_rand_ns(rng)))

    # Include hex strings (with and without 0x)
    pieces.append(_ensure_nul_terminated(_rand_hex(rng, with_prefix_prob=1.0)))
    pieces.append(_ensure_nul_terminated(_rand_hex(rng, with_prefix_prob=0.0)))

    # Include a plausible file path
    pieces.append(_ensure_nul_terminated(_rand_cstring(rng if rng.random()<1 else rng)))

    # Include printf-safe payload
    pieces.append(_ensure_nul_terminated(_rand_printf_payload(rng)))

    # Include a module name and a keyword
    pieces.append(_ensure_nul_terminated(_rand_cstring(rng)))
    pieces.append(_ensure_nul_terminated(_rand_cstring(rng)))

    # Add a medium random printable block
    pieces.append(_ensure_nul_terminated(_rand_cstring(rng)))

    # Concatenate while respecting MAX_TOTAL
    out = bytearray()
    for p in pieces:
        if len(out) + len(p) <= MAX_TOTAL:
            out.extend(p)
        else:
            break

    # Ensure at least one NUL present
    if not out or out[-1] != 0:
        out.append(0)

    return bytes(out)

import random

# Utility helpers

def _rand_ascii(r: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    length = r.randint(min_len, max_len)
    alphabet = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789_-.:/\\ " + "\t\r\n"

def _make_wide(s: bytes) -> bytes:
    out = bytearray()
    for b in s:
        out.append(b)
        out.append(0)
    out.extend(b"\x00\x00")
    return bytes(out)

def _to_base64(data: bytes) -> bytes:
    import binascii
    return binascii.b2a_base64(data).strip()

# Variants

def _variant_text(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    parts: List[bytes] = []
    headers = [b"MZ\x90\x00", b"\x7fELF", b"PK\x03\x04", b"%PDF-", b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n"]
    parts.append(r.choice(headers) + b"\n")
    for _ in range(r.randint(3, 8)):
        parts.append(_rand_ascii(r, 5, 40).encode("ascii") + b"\n")
    hexline = (" ".join(f"{r.randrange(0,256):02x}" for _ in range(r.randint(8, 32)))).encode()
    parts.append(b"hex: " + hexline + b"\n")

    parts.append(b"b64: " + _to_base64(raw) + b"\n")
    parts.append(b"WIDE:\n" + _make_wide(b"wide_string_example") + b"\n")
    token = r.choice([b"AAAA", b"abcd", b"XYZ", b"malware"])
    parts.append(token * r.randint(3, 20) + b"\n")

def _variant_entropy_blob(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    size = r.randint(256, min(2048, MAX_SIZE))
    data = bytearray(r.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(size))
    markers = [b"MZ", b"\x7fELF", b"PE\x00\x00", b"YARA", b"RULE", b"SCANNING"]
    for m in markers:
        off = r.randint(0, max(0, size - len(m)))
        data[off:off+len(m)] = m
    raw = bytes(r.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(48))

    ins = r.randint(0, max(0, size - len(b64)))

def _variant_minimal_pe(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # DOS header up to e_lfanew
    mz = bytearray()
    mz.extend(b"MZ")
    mz.extend(b"\x90\x00\x03\x00\x00\x00\x04\x00\x00\x00\xFF\xFF\x00\x00\xB8\x00\x00\x00")
    while len(mz) < 0x3C:
        mz.append(0)
    e_lfanew = 0x80
    mz.extend(struct.pack('<I', e_lfanew))
    while len(mz) < e_lfanew:
        mz.append(0)

    # PE signature and COFF header
    pe = bytearray()
    pe.extend(b"PE\x00\x00")
    Machine = 0x014C
    NumberOfSections = 1
    TimeDateStamp = r.getrandbits(32)
    PointerToSymbolTable = 0
    NumberOfSymbols = 0
    SizeOfOptionalHeader = 224  # PE32
    Characteristics = 0x010F
    pe.extend(struct.pack('<HHIIIHH', Machine, NumberOfSections, TimeDateStamp,
                          PointerToSymbolTable, NumberOfSymbols,
                          SizeOfOptionalHeader, Characteristics))

    # Optional Header (PE32) - pack in segments to avoid mismatched counts
    Magic = 0x10B
    MajorLinkerVersion = 14
    MinorLinkerVersion = 0
    SizeOfCode = 0x200
    SizeOfInitializedData = 0x200
    SizeOfUninitializedData = 0
    AddressOfEntryPoint = 0x1000
    BaseOfCode = 0x1000
    BaseOfData = 0x2000
    ImageBase = 0x400000
    SectionAlignment = 0x1000
    FileAlignment = 0x200
    MajorOS = 6; MinorOS = 0
    MajorImg = 0; MinorImg = 0
    MajorSub = 6; MinorSub = 0
    Win32VersionValue = 0
    SizeOfImage = 0x4000
    SizeOfHeaders = 0x200
    CheckSum = 0
    Subsystem = 3
    DllCharacteristics = 0
    SizeOfStackReserve = 0x100000
    SizeOfStackCommit = 0x1000
    SizeOfHeapReserve = 0x100000
    SizeOfHeapCommit = 0x1000
    LoaderFlags = 0
    NumberOfRvaAndSizes = 16

    # Fields before ImageBase
    opt1 = struct.pack('<HBBIIIIII', Magic, MajorLinkerVersion, MinorLinkerVersion,
                       SizeOfCode, SizeOfInitializedData, SizeOfUninitializedData,
                       AddressOfEntryPoint, BaseOfCode, BaseOfData)
    # Windows-specific fields up to DllCharacteristics
    opt2 = struct.pack('<IIIIHHHHIIIIH', ImageBase, SectionAlignment, FileAlignment,
                       MajorOS, MinorOS, MajorImg, MinorImg, MajorSub, MinorSub,
                       Win32VersionValue, SizeOfImage, SizeOfHeaders, CheckSum)
    # Subsystem, DllCharacteristics, sizes and flags
    opt3 = struct.pack('<HHIIIIII', Subsystem, DllCharacteristics, SizeOfStackReserve,
                       SizeOfStackCommit, SizeOfHeapReserve, SizeOfHeapCommit,
                       LoaderFlags, NumberOfRvaAndSizes)

    pe.extend(opt1)
    pe.extend(opt2)
    pe.extend(opt3)

    # Data directories (zero)
    pe.extend(b"\x00" * (8 * NumberOfRvaAndSizes))

    # Section header (.text)
    name = b".text\x00\x00\x00"
    VirtualSize = 0x1000
    VirtualAddress = 0x1000
    SizeOfRawData = 0x200
    PointerToRawData = 0x200
    PointerToRelocations = 0
    PointerToLinenumbers = 0
    NumberOfRelocations = 0
    NumberOfLinenumbers = 0
    SectCharacteristics = 0x60000020
    sect = struct.pack('<8sIIIIIIHHI', name, VirtualSize, VirtualAddress,
                       SizeOfRawData, PointerToRawData, PointerToRelocations,
                       PointerToLinenumbers, NumberOfRelocations,
                       NumberOfLinenumbers, SectCharacteristics)
    pe.extend(sect)

    # Assemble file
    file = bytearray(mz)
    file.extend(pe)
    if len(file) < 0x200:
        file.extend(b"\x00" * (0x200 - len(file)))

    text = bytearray(b"\x31\xC0\xC3")  # xor eax,eax; ret
    if len(text) < SizeOfRawData:
        text.extend(b"\x90" * (SizeOfRawData - len(text)))
    file.extend(text)
    return bytes(file[:MAX_SIZE])

    e_ident.extend(b"\x00" * 8)

    e_machine = 0x3E
    e_version = 1
    e_entry = 0x400080
    e_phoff = 64
    e_shoff = 0
    e_flags = 0
    e_ehsize = 64
    e_phentsize = 56
    e_phnum = 1
    e_shentsize = 64
    e_shnum = 0
    e_shstrndx = 0
    hdr = struct.pack('<16sHHIQQQIHHHHHH', bytes(e_ident), e_type, e_machine, e_version,
                      e_entry, e_phoff, e_shoff, e_flags, e_ehsize, e_phentsize,
                      e_phnum, e_shentsize, e_shnum, e_shstrndx)
    p_type = 1
    p_flags = 5
    p_offset = 0
    p_vaddr = 0x400000
    p_paddr = 0x400000
    p_filesz = 0x200
    p_memsz = 0x200
    p_align = 0x200000
    ph = struct.pack('<IIQQQQQQ', p_type, p_flags, p_offset, p_vaddr, p_paddr,

    code = bytearray(b"\xC3")
    if len(code) < p_filesz:
        code.extend(b"\x00" * (p_filesz - len(code)))
    blob = hdr + ph + code

def _variant_quality_table_like(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    recs = r.randint(8, 32)
    buf = bytearray()
    for _ in range(recs):
        atom = bytes(r.randrange(0, 256) for _ in range(32))
        quality = r.randrange(0, 256)
        buf.extend(atom)
        buf.append(quality)
    return bytes(buf[:MAX_SIZE])

def _choose_variant(r: random.Random):
    choices = [
        (_variant_text, 35),
        (_variant_entropy_blob, 25),
        (_variant_minimal_pe, 15),
        (_variant_minimal_elf64, 15),
        (_variant_quality_table_like, 10),
    ]
    total = sum(w for _, w in choices)
    pick = r.randrange(total)
    acc = 0
    for fn, w in choices:
        acc += w
        if pick < acc:
            return fn
    return choices[0][0]

# Public API

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    variant = _choose_variant(r)
    data = variant(r)
    if not data:
        data = b"A"
    if len(data) > MAX_SIZE:
        data = data[:MAX_SIZE]
    return data

import random

import string
from typing import Tuple

# Data type: alphanumeric identifier (letters, digits, underscore), typically not starting with a digit.
# Fuzzer stubs use FUZZ_PARAM_STR twice to generate:
#  - an identifier (sanitized to [A-Za-z0-9_], max 32 chars, and not starting with a digit; fallback ids: "flt"/"str")
#  - a value string (any bytes, but provided as C string in stub)
# They also use a FUZZ_PARAM(uint64_t) to form a finite double.
#
# Goal: produce a seedable bytes buffer that, when consumed by the fuzz harness,
# yields interesting but valid inputs:
#  - Provide multiple candidate identifiers (varied lengths, with/without leading digits) so sanitizer paths differ.
#  - Include candidates that already valid and those that force fallback to "flt"/"str".
#  - Provide varied string payloads: ASCII, Unicode bytes, long/short, with NUL avoidance since FUZZ_PARAM_STR expects std::string.
#  - Provide several uint64_t patterns to generate finite doubles of diverse magnitudes/signs.
#
# We do not know exact FUZZ_PARAM wire format. Typical fuzz frameworks read sequentially from a byte buffer.
# We'll construct a simple concatenation of sections the fuzzer can sample from:
# [header magic][count fields][identifiers blob][string values blob][u64 values blob]
# Even if the harness picks slices arbitrarily, embedding many valid options increases chance of valid consumption.

MAX_TOTAL_SIZE = 4096

ALNUM = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_"


def rand_identifier(r: random.Random, min_len: int = 1, max_len: int = 32, allow_leading_digit: bool = False) -> str:
    L = r.randint(min_len, max_len)
    if not allow_leading_digit:
        first = r.choice(string.ascii_letters + "_")
    else:
        first = r.choice(ALNUM)
    rest = "".join(r.choice(ALNUM) for _ in range(max(0, L - 1)))
    return first + rest


def make_maybe_invalid_identifier(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Sometimes start with digit or insert non-identifier chars to trigger sanitizer and fallbacks
    modes = [
        "valid",
        "leading_digit",
        "non_alnum_mix",
        "empty",
        "too_long",
    ]
    mode = r.choice(modes)
    if mode == "valid":
        return rand_identifier(r)
    if mode == "leading_digit":
        L = r.randint(1, 32)
        first = r.choice(string.digits)
        rest = "".join(r.choice(ALNUM) for _ in range(max(0, L - 1)))
        return first + rest
    if mode == "non_alnum_mix":
        base = rand_identifier(r)
        inserts = "-:+./\\@#%$!^&*()[]{}|?~,;\n\t"
        pos = r.randint(0, len(base))
        return base[:pos] + r.choice(inserts) + base[pos:]
    if mode == "empty":
        return ""
    if mode == "too_long":
        # Over 32 to exercise truncation
        return rand_identifier(r, min_len=33, max_len=64, allow_leading_digit=r.choice([True, False]))
    return rand_identifier(r)


def make_value_string(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Produce diverse strings: ASCII, mixed unicode bytes, repeated patterns.
    kinds = ["ascii", "alnum", "unicode_bytes", "hex_like", "long_ascii", "short", "wideish"]
    kind = r.choice(kinds)
    if kind == "ascii":
        L = r.randint(1, 64)
        s = "".join(r.choice(string.printable[:-6]) for _ in range(L))
        return s.encode("utf-8", errors="ignore")
    if kind == "alnum":
        L = r.randint(1, 48)
        s = "".join(r.choice(ALNUM) for _ in range(L))
        return s.encode()
    if kind == "unicode_bytes":
        L = r.randint(4, 80)
        # Build bytes in ranges covering UTF-8 multi-byte sequences and raw bytes
        b = bytearray()
        for _ in range(L):
            b.append(r.choice([r.randint(0x20, 0x7E), r.randint(0xC2, 0xF4), r.randint(0x80, 0xBF)]))
        # Avoid embedded NUL in std::string by replacing 0 with space
        return bytes(x if x != 0 else 0x20 for x in b)
    if kind == "hex_like":
        L = r.randint(2, 64)
        s = "".join(r.choice("0123456789abcdef ") for _ in range(L))
        return s.encode()
    if kind == "long_ascii":
        L = r.randint(80, 256)
        s = ("A1_" * ((L + 2) // 3))[:L]
        return s.encode()
    if kind == "short":
        return r.choice([b"", b"a", b"0", b"_"])
    if kind == "wideish":
        base = "".join(r.choice(string.ascii_letters) for _ in range(r.randint(2, 24)))
        # Interleave with zero bytes removed (use \x01 instead of \x00 to stay non-NUL)
        out = bytearray()
        for ch in base.encode():
            out.append(ch)
            out.append(1)
        return bytes(out)
    return b""


def make_finite_double_bits_list(r: random.Random, count: int) -> bytes:
    # Provide a sequence of uint64_t values whose doubles are finite and diverse
    out = bytearray()
    for _ in range(count):
        choice = r.randint(0, 6)
        if choice == 0:
            # Small integers exactly representable
            v = r.randint(-1000000, 1000000)
            bits = struct.unpack("<Q", struct.pack("<d", float(v)))[0]
        elif choice == 1:
            # Subnormal-ish small magnitude
            mant = r.getrandbits(52)
            exp = 0  # subnormal when exp == 0 and mant != 0
            sign = r.getrandbits(1)
            bits = (sign << 63) | (exp << 52) | (mant & ((1<<52)-1))
        elif choice == 2:
            # Normal with moderate exponent
            mant = r.getrandbits(52)
            exp = r.randint(1, 2045)  # avoid 2047 (Inf/NaN), avoid 0 here
            sign = r.getrandbits(1)
            bits = (sign << 63) | (exp << 52) | (mant & ((1<<52)-1))
        elif choice == 3:
            # Powers of two
            exp = r.randint(1, 1022)
            sign = r.getrandbits(1)
            bits = (sign << 63) | (exp << 52)
        elif choice == 4:
            # Fractions between 0 and 1
            f = r.random()
            bits = struct.unpack("<Q", struct.pack("<d", f))[0]
        elif choice == 5:
            # Large finite
            f = r.uniform(-1e300, 1e300)
            bits = struct.unpack("<Q", struct.pack("<d", f))[0]
        else:
            # Exact decimal fractions that are non-terminating in binary
            f = r.choice([0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 1/3, 2/3, 10/3, 1.5, -2.5])
            bits = struct.unpack("<Q", struct.pack("<d", float(f)))[0]
        # Ensure not NaN/Inf: clear all-ones exponent if it accidentally occurs
        if ((bits >> 52) & 0x7FF) == 0x7FF:
            bits &= 0x0FFFFFFFFFFFFFFF
        out += struct.pack("<Q", bits)
    return bytes(out)


def build_section(prefix: bytes, items: Tuple[bytes, ...]) -> bytes:
    blob = bytearray()
    blob += prefix
    blob += struct.pack("<H", len(items))
    for it in items:
        blob += struct.pack("<H", len(it))
        blob += it
    return bytes(blob)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)

    # Prepare a bunch of candidate identifiers (for both float and string stubs)
    id_count = r.randint(6, 14)
    ids = []
    for _ in range(id_count):
        ids.append(make_maybe_invalid_identifier(r).encode("utf-8", errors="ignore"))
    # Ensure we include at least one clearly valid and one clearly invalid
    ids.append(rand_identifier(r).encode())
    ids.append((r.choice(string.digits) + "bad").encode())

    # Prepare value strings
    val_count = r.randint(6, 14)
    vals = []
    for _ in range(val_count):
        v = make_value_string(r)
        # Avoid embedded NUL for safer std::string construction
        v = v.replace(b"\x00", b" ")
        vals.append(v)
    # Add some well-known tokens
    vals += [b"", b"hello", b"YARA_var_123", b"ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789_"]

    # Prepare a series of uint64_t values for doubles
    u64_blob = make_finite_double_bits_list(r, count=r.randint(8, 24))

    # Build sections
    header = b"YG\x01\x00"  # simple magic/version
    id_section = build_section(b"ID", tuple(ids))
    val_section = build_section(b"SV", tuple(vals))
    u64_section = b"D8" + struct.pack("<H", len(u64_blob) // 8) + u64_blob

    out = header + id_section + val_section + u64_section
    if len(out) > MAX_TOTAL_SIZE:
        out = out[:MAX_TOTAL_SIZE]
    return bytes(out)

import struct
import string

# Target: yr_rules_define_float_variable fuzzer stub expects:
# - FUZZ_PARAM(uint64_t): raw 64-bit used to craft a finite double (stub masks)
# - FUZZ_PARAM_STR(): identifier candidate (alnum/underscore, first not digit, max 32)
# We should return bytes that the fuzzer harness will slice to satisfy these in order.
# Assumption: The harness consumes from the provided buffer sequentially.

IDENT_CHOICES = [
    "flt",                 # simple default identifier
    "pi_value",            # letters and underscore
    "X1_",                 # starts with letter, includes digit and underscore
    "temperature_celsius", # longer identifier
    "var1234567890",       # mixed with digits
    "_underscore",         # starts with underscore is allowed
]

# Interesting finite doubles to exercise code paths after mask is applied.
# We'll directly provide uint64_t bit patterns that decode to these doubles
# even after the stub applies: bits &= 0x0FFFFFFFFFFFFFFF (clear top 4 bits of MS nybble)
# However, since the stub writes the bits directly to a union double, we can just encode
# desired doubles; the mask will keep them finite anyway.
INTERESTING_DOUBLES = [
    0.0,
    -0.0,
    1.0,
    -1.0,
    3.141592653589793,
    2.718281828459045,
    1e-308,   # tiny normal/subnormal boundary region
    1e308,    # large finite
    -1e308,
    123456.789,
]


def _pack_uint64_from_double(d: float) -> bytes:
    # Pack a Python float into uint64 bits (IEEE-754) in native endianness of the fuzzer
    # Use little-endian for portability; most fuzz harnesses read as host-endian, but
    # FUZZ_PARAM(uint64_t) likely reads 8 bytes as-is. We'll emit little-endian as common.
    bits = struct.unpack('<Q', struct.pack('<d', d))[0]
    return struct.pack('<Q', bits)


def _build_identifier(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Choose from curated identifiers and sometimes synthesize random valid ones
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        ident = rng.choice(IDENT_CHOICES)
    else:
        length = rng.randint(1, 24)
        first_chars = string.ascii_letters + "_"
        rest_chars = first_chars + string.digits
        ident = rng.choice(first_chars)
        ident += ''.join(rng.choice(rest_chars) for _ in range(length - 1))
    # FUZZ_PARAM_STR returns arbitrary bytes; but stub filters to [A-Za-z0-9_], and then
    # checks first char isn't a digit; otherwise uses "flt". We'll provide exactly the
    # identifier so it passes filtering as-is.
    return ident.encode('ascii')


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # 1) Provide 8 bytes for FUZZ_PARAM(uint64_t): craft a finite double bits
    d = rng.choice(INTERESTING_DOUBLES)
    # Occasionally choose a random finite in range, to diversify
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        # Uniform in a moderate finite range
        d = rng.uniform(-1e300, 1e300)
    bits_le = _pack_uint64_from_double(d)

    # 2) Provide bytes for FUZZ_PARAM_STR(): identifier candidate
    ident_bytes = _build_identifier(rng)

    # Concatenate. Keep under 4096 bytes easily.
    # If the harness expects length-prefixed strings, FUZZ_PARAM_STR typically
    # slices from remaining bytes using an internal length; since we cannot know,
    # we simply place the string directly after the 8-byte integer so that
    # the fuzzer library can consume it as needed. Many fuzzers use internal
    # delimiters or sizes; to increase robustness, we append a NUL terminator.
    buf = bytearray()
    buf += bits_le
    buf += ident_bytes
    buf += b"\x00"

    return bytes(buf)

import random
import struct
import string

# This generator targets fuzzer stubs that call:
#   - FUZZ_PARAM_STR()  -> used as identifier for yr_scanner_define_float_variable
#   - FUZZ_PARAM(double) -> used as the floating-point value
# Goal: produce a buffer that decodes into a non-empty identifier string and a
# interesting double value. The harness typically reads items sequentially from
# the provided buffer, so we encode as:
#   [u16 id_len][id_bytes][u8 float_kind][double_payload]
# Where:
# - id_len: 2-byte big-endian length of the identifier string
# - id_bytes: UTF-8/ASCII bytes of identifier, no NULs
# - float_kind: selector to produce diverse doubles
# - double_payload: 8 bytes representing IEEE-754 double in native endianness
# Keep total <= 4096 bytes.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

# A set of plausible YARA identifier characters: [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*
LETTERS = string.ascii_letters + "_"
IDENT_TAIL = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_"


def _rand_identifier(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Choose among interesting identifiers that may trigger internal lookups,
    # or random valid identifiers.
    specials = [
        "pe", "elf", "math", "time", "filesize", "entrypoint",
        "version", "pid", "tid", "myVar", "foo", "bar",
    ]
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        return rng.choice(specials)
    # otherwise craft a random valid identifier length 1..32
    length = rng.randint(1, 32)
    head = rng.choice(LETTERS)
    tail = "".join(rng.choice(IDENT_TAIL) for _ in range(length - 1))
    return head + tail


def _interesting_double(rng: random.Random) -> float:
    # Return diverse doubles including edge cases and random normals
    kinds = [
        "zero", "neg_zero", "small", "large", "pi", "e", "rand", "subnormal",
        "nan", "inf", "ninf"
    ]
    kind = rng.choice(kinds)
    if kind == "zero":
        return 0.0
    if kind == "neg_zero":
        return struct.unpack('>d', b"\x80\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00")[0]
    if kind == "small":
        return rng.choice([1e-308, 5e-324, 2.2250738585072014e-308])
    if kind == "large":
        return rng.choice([1e308, 1.79e308, 3.402823669209385e38])
    if kind == "pi":
        return 3.141592653589793
    if kind == "e":
        return 2.718281828459045
    if kind == "subnormal":
        # Construct a random subnormal: exponent=0, nonzero mantissa
        mant = rng.getrandbits(52)
        if mant == 0:
            mant = 1
        bits = mant  # sign=0, exp=0
        return struct.unpack('>d', bits.to_bytes(8, 'big'))[0]
    if kind == "nan":
        # quiet NaN payload
        return float('nan')
    if kind == "inf":
        return float('inf')
    if kind == "ninf":
        return float('-inf')
    # rand normal finite
    sign = -1.0 if rng.random() < 0.5 else 1.0
    exp = rng.uniform(-300.0, 300.0)
    base = rng.uniform(0.0, 1.0)
    val = sign * (10.0 ** exp) * (base if base > 1e-12 else 1.0)
    # clamp to finite range
    if not (val == val) or val == float('inf') or val == float('-inf'):
        val = rng.uniform(-1e100, 1e100)
    return val


def _pack_double_native(d: float) -> bytes:
    # Pack in native endianness as many fuzz harnesses read double directly.
    return struct.pack('=d', d)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    ident = _rand_identifier(rng)

    # Ensure non-empty and reasonable size
    ident_bytes = ident.encode('utf-8', 'ignore')[:255]
    if not ident_bytes:
        ident_bytes = b"x"

    d = _interesting_double(rng)

    # Build buffer: [u16be len][id][u8 kind hint][double native]
    # kind hint is just a random byte; consumers that ignore it will still parse id then double bytes.
    buf = bytearray()
    buf += struct.pack('>H', len(ident_bytes))
    buf += ident_bytes
    buf += struct.pack('B', rng.randrange(0, 256))
    buf += _pack_double_native(d)

    # Ensure we do not exceed limit
    return bytes(buf[:MAX_TOTAL])

import random

HEX_DIGITS_LOWER = "0123456789abcdef"
HEX_DIGITS_UPPER = "0123456789ABCDEF"

def _rand_hex_str(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int, allow_prefix: bool) -> str:
    length = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    # Mix upper and lower to exercise both cases
    digits_pool = HEX_DIGITS_LOWER + HEX_DIGITS_UPPER
    s = ''.join(rng.choice(digits_pool) for _ in range(length))
    if allow_prefix and rng.choice([True, False]):
        s = rng.choice(['0x', '0X']) + s
    return s

def _biased_lengths(seed: int) -> List[int]:
    # Provide interesting lengths including edge-ish values
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    choices = [1, 2, 3, 7, 8, 15, 16, 31, 32, 63, 64]
    # Add a couple random ones up to a few hundred
    choices += [rng.randint(5, 120), rng.randint(121, 512)]
    return choices

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Build a corpus of diverse valid hex strings
    parts: List[str] = []

    # 1) Simple single-digit values
    parts.append(rng.choice(HEX_DIGITS_LOWER))
    parts.append(rng.choice(HEX_DIGITS_UPPER))

    # 2) With 0x/0X prefixes
    parts.append('0x' + ''.join(rng.choice(HEX_DIGITS_LOWER) for _ in range(1)))
    parts.append('0X' + ''.join(rng.choice(HEX_DIGITS_UPPER) for _ in range(2)))

    # 3) Mixed-case long numbers exercising overflow paths (up to 64 hex digits ~ 256 bits)
    for L in _biased_lengths(seed):
        parts.append(_rand_hex_str(rng, L, L, allow_prefix=True))

    # 4) Edge cases: leading zeros, very long sequence, alternating case
    parts.append('0x' + '0' * rng.randint(1, 10) + '1')
    alt = ''.join((HEX_DIGITS_LOWER[i % 16] if (i % 2 == 0) else HEX_DIGITS_UPPER[i % 16]) for i in range(rng.randint(16, 64)))
    parts.append(alt)

    # 5) Random additional samples
    for _ in range(rng.randint(3, 8)):
        parts.append(_rand_hex_str(rng, 1, 80, allow_prefix=True))

    # Join samples with newlines so the fuzzer can pick substrings or provide as a file buffer as needed.
    # Each line is a valid, NUL-free C string and can be fed directly to xtoi.
    payload = ("\n".join(parts) + "\n").encode('ascii')

    # Ensure we do not exceed 4096 bytes
    return payload[:4096]

import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator produces valid YARA wide strings (ASCII bytes interleaved with 0x00,
# terminated by two consecutive 0x00). The fuzz stubs build their own wide strings from
# FUZZ_PARAM_STR, but seeding them with already wide-looking data helps exercise edge cases
# like empty strings, long strings, mixed cases, prefixes/suffixes, and embedded null-safe
# characters. We mix a small set of crafted ASCII strings with random ASCII to broaden
# coverage. The output is a single bytes buffer; fuzz harness will split or reuse it as needed.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

ASCII_POOL = (
    ["", "A", "B", "C", "hello", "world", "test", "wide", "YARA", "fuzz"]
    + ["a" * n for n in (1, 2, 3, 7, 15, 31, 63, 127, 255)]
    + ["ab" * n for n in (1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32)]
    + ["The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog"]
    + ["0123456789", "!@#$%^&*()-_=+[]{};:'\",.<>/?|`~"]
)

def to_yara_wide(ascii_s: str) -> bytes:
    # Replace embedded NULs if any (though we avoid generating them) to ensure validity
    ascii_clean = ascii_s.replace("\x00", "_")
    out = bytearray()
    for ch in ascii_clean.encode('latin1', 'ignore'):
        out.append(ch)
        out.append(0)
    # double NUL terminator
    out.append(0)
    out.append(0)
    return bytes(out)

def rand_ascii(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    # Use visible ASCII plus space; avoid NULs
    alphabet = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + string.punctuation + " "
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return "".join(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n))

def build_interesting_set(rng: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    items: List[bytes] = []

    # Corner cases
    items.append(to_yara_wide(""))                 # empty -> immediate double NUL
    items.append(to_yara_wide("\u00FF"))          # non-ASCII byte via latin1 (will encode as 0xFF)
    items.append(to_yara_wide("0"))
    items.append(to_yara_wide("A"))
    items.append(to_yara_wide("AB"))
    items.append(to_yara_wide("AAA"))

    # Typical words
    for s in ("hello", "Hello", "HELLO", "yara", "YARA", "wide", "string", "comparison"):
        items.append(to_yara_wide(s))

    # Repeated patterns
    for rep in (1, 2, 3, 5, 10):
        items.append(to_yara_wide("ab" * rep))
        items.append(to_yara_wide("ABC" * rep))

    # Longish sequences near caps used in stubs (512 characters)
    items.append(to_yara_wide("x" * 511))
    items.append(to_yara_wide("y" * 512))
    items.append(to_yara_wide("z" * 513))

    # From pool
    for s in ASCII_POOL[:20]:
        items.append(to_yara_wide(s))

    # Random selections of varying sizes
    for _ in range(12):
        items.append(to_yara_wide(rand_ascii(rng, 1, 40)))
    for _ in range(6):
        items.append(to_yara_wide(rand_ascii(rng, 80, 140)))

    # Mixed punctuation-heavy samples
    for _ in range(4):
        s = "".join(rng.choice("!@#$%^&*()_+-=[]{};:',.<>/?|`~") for _ in range(rng.randint(5, 25)))
        items.append(to_yara_wide(s))

    # Case-variation pairs to exercise strcmp_w code paths
    base = rand_ascii(rng, 5, 15)
    items.append(to_yara_wide(base))
    items.append(to_yara_wide(base.lower()))
    items.append(to_yara_wide(base.upper()))

    return items

def pack_multi_wide_chunks(chunks: List[bytes], max_total: int, rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Concatenate multiple wide strings separated by an extra double-NUL gap, still valid individual items.
    out = bytearray()
    for chunk in chunks:
        # Ensure we respect max_total size
        if len(out) + len(chunk) > max_total:
            break
        out += chunk
        # Optional additional separator (another double NUL) to delimit segments
        if rng.random() < 0.3 and len(out) + 2 <= max_total:
            out += b"\x00\x00"
    # Guarantee buffer is non-empty and ends with a double NUL terminator sequence
    if not out:
        out = bytearray(to_yara_wide(""))
    else:
        # Ensure last two bytes are NULs (valid wide termination at end)
        if len(out) < 2 or out[-2:] != b"\x00\x00":
            if len(out) + 2 <= max_total:
                out += b"\x00\x00"
            else:
                # Trim last 2 and append proper terminator
                if len(out) >= 2:
                    out[-2:] = b"\x00\x00"
                else:
                    out = bytearray(b"\x00\x00")
    return bytes(out)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Build a pool of valid wide strings
    items = build_interesting_set(rng)

    # Shuffle to vary coverage
    rng.shuffle(items)

    # Select a random number of chunks to concatenate, ensuring interesting variety
    k = rng.randint(3, min(12, len(items)))
    chosen = items[:k]

    buf = pack_multi_wide_chunks(chosen, MAX_TOTAL, rng)

    # Final safety: limit size to 4096 bytes
    if len(buf) > MAX_TOTAL:
        buf = buf[:MAX_TOTAL]
        # Try to keep it validly terminated
        if len(buf) >= 2:
            buf = buf[:-2] + b"\x00\x00"
        else:
            buf = b"\x00\x00"

    return buf
